related_titles_screened.title: For every positive modulus, sufficiently high distinct-wise intersection divisibility bounds a set family by two to the floor of n divided by the modulus plus a constant, with no constant for large divisible n

independence: Only original Theorem 1 is selected: every positive modulus, a sufficiently high distinct-wise intersection requirement depending on that modulus, every positive ground-set size, the exact additive constant, and its disappearance for sufficiently large divisible sizes. The full authored small-doubling theorem with all three fully editable matrix illustrations, prime-power lifting, repeated squaring, atomic closed-family theorem, Oddtown variant, matching removal and main closing are included. Ordinary prerequisites are basic linear algebra over finite fields/modular rings, elementary prime-power congruences, and Odlyzko [17] Boolean-points bound stated as Lemma 14. Freiman/Ruzsa approximate-group references in the introduction are positioning only and are not proof prerequisites. Source statement/proof literals such as the scalar count d-h in Lemma 11, the base-case product notation and the unprimed S/A-prime construction at main closing are preserved unchanged. Unselected stability and dimension variants are not counted; their omitted counters are restored so all original selected indices remain exact.
